findings.reason: §7 must either name the extension to `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py` (a record-shape-general cache) or drop the reuse claim and declare a separate store, because the reuse it asserts is not possible as written.
findings.text: §7 says the EQDB reader uses the §3 extractor's "transport and cache rather than a second path", but `fetch_channels` is typed `extractor: RemoteEddbExtractor` (imas_ambix/data/eddb.py:278) and `write_channel` persists a `ChannelRecord` whose layout is a `(nch, ntime)` time-series keyed `{int(shot)}.zarr/{category}/{dname}` with a sibling time array; an EQDB equilibrium record is a 2-D psi snapshot on a grid with no single time axis, so it cannot ride that cache, and the plan's own open question `eqdb-reader` concedes the record shape is unknown. The node's brief would otherwise build a fetch entry that cannot write through the cited cache.

findings.reason: under the one rule for interface-budget sections, §3 must add a sentence accounting for the interface it introduced (the extractor/cache surface and the two error families), so the added surface is visible in the plan rather than only in the merged code.
findings.text: §3 (measured additions public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0) lands two new public modules, `imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py` (public `RemoteEddbExtractor`, `BatchResult`, `ChannelRecord`, `ChannelRefusal`, `ChannelRequest`, `SshTransport`, `Transport`, `fetch_batch`) and `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py` (public `fetch_channels`, `write_channel`, `is_cached`, `channel_path`, `time_array_name`, …), plus two new refusal families `EddbRemoteError` and `EddbCacheError`, yet the section's own text names no public surface retired or merged and says nothing about why there is none.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new units hide substantial behaviour behind small interfaces: one converter entry point (`imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py`) parsing three deck grammars into five IDS netCDF, and one exporter function (`export_tokamap_directory`, imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py:349) collapsing unit×sign×COCOS over every binding. No design is spread across shallow wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 claims the EQDB reader reuses "its transport and cache rather than a second path", but the §3 cache is owned by `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py` and is EDDB-time-series-specific.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 (supplied); §3's access path adds two public modules and two refusal families without a retirement or merge statement in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase it names and cites each mechanism it extends (MAST's 254-binding map and level-2 store, the nakamap deck seed it explicitly supersedes, existing `load_packaged_signal_map`/`load_machine_map` loaders, `transform_engine`/`description_reader`, `cocos_convention.py`, `challenge/convention.py`, `eval/efit_referee.judge_geometry`, `gs/artifact_resolution.py`), rather than proposing parallel machinery.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — where the plan adds a layer it names why the owner cannot be extended and then extends the owner: `StoreEngine.open` gains the selected map (`imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:413` already holds the map), `read_geometry_table`'s machine branch is replaced by a catalogue-declared `probe_angle_source` (verified: `_supply_declared_probe_angles` is now gated on `probe_angle_source == "acquisition-address"`, no `machine ==` branch), and `measure_diiid_convention` is generalised through a loader contract rather than joined by a second scorer.
